comingSoon.accounts: Create hosting accounts from a plan: a Linux user with its disk quota, its sites, domains, mailboxes and databases.
comingSoon.databases: Start MariaDB, MySQL or PostgreSQL instances per account on demand, with their databases and users.
comingSoon.domains: Manage main, addon and alias domains, subdomains and their DNS zones, with automatic TLS certificates.
comingSoon.files: Browse and edit the files of an account, and open an SFTP/FTPS server on demand for it.
comingSoon.mail: Manage mailboxes, aliases, forwards, quotas and DKIM keys on the mail engine chosen at installation.
comingSoon.plans: Define hosting plans (disk, traffic, sites, mailboxes, databases…) within the resource envelope of the workspace.
comingSoon.sites: Deploy each site in its own container with the base of your choice (PHP, Node.js, static…), immutable code and a controlled update window.

fix.datadir_fs: Without XFS and the prjquota mount option, disk quotas are only measured, not enforced. Put /srv/oblimint on an XFS volume mounted with prjquota.
fix.docker: Install or upgrade Docker Engine to version 24 or later, then restart the container.
fix.os: Oblimint is tested on Debian, AlmaLinux and Rocky Linux. Other systems may work but are not supported.
fix.ports: Stop the service that uses the port (another web, DNS or mail server), then run the checks again. Ports 53 and 25 only have to be freed before the DNS and mail modules are enabled.
fix.resources: At least 2 CPU cores and 4 GB of RAM are recommended.
fix.self: Start the container with the Docker socket and /srv/oblimint mounted, as shown in the installation command.
fix.selinux: With SELinux enforcing, label the data directory for containers (see the command).

dms.cons: Driven through files and CLI (no API); big monolithic container.
dms.pros: Postfix/Dovecot/Rspamd already assembled and proven in one widely used container.

external.name: None (external)
external.pros: Customers use Google Workspace, Microsoft 365 or another server: the panel only manages the DNS records (MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC).

maddy.cons: Small community, basic antispam, few hosting features.
maddy.pros: Very light single Go binary, simple configuration.

postfix.cons: 4–5 components to configure and upgrade together; the heaviest with antispam.
postfix.pros: The 20-year standard, rock solid and documented everywhere; same as CWP (Maildir and password hashes reused as is).

stalwart.cons: Younger: less production hindsight, smaller community; some advanced features under an enterprise licence.
stalwart.pros: Modern all-in-one (SMTP, IMAP, JMAP, POP3, antispam, DKIM), administration API, lightweight single binary.
